section_summary: This section contains diplomatic and departmental correspondence, legal opinions, staff studies, directives, and background monographs concerning Japanese nationality and personal status issues during the Allied occupation. Key matters include procedures for the renunciation and recovery of Japanese citizenship by dual nationals, the issuance of certificates of nationality and travel documents to Japanese subjects and Ryukyuans abroad, and proposed postal communication mechanisms between Japan and overseas residents. The records also address the legal, civil, and property status of Japanese nationals remaining in detached territories such as Korea, Formosa, Saghalien, and the Kuriles, as well as Koreans and Formosans residing in post-war Japan.

subfiles.about: This staff study recommends permitting direct international postal communication between the Japanese government and overseas residents to resolve approximately 700,000 personal status cases.
subfiles.from: Diplomatic Section, Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.summary: This staff study examines the administrative and legal difficulties resulting from existing SCAP prohibitions on international mail concerning personal status matters, which have left approximately 700,000 cases involving overseas Japanese unresolved. It argues that direct postal communication is legally permissible under Allied policy, would prevent hardship regarding nationality and property rights, and would not undermine Japanese land reform programs. The study recommends issuing a SCAP directive authorizing direct correspondence and public information on family registration and nationality matters, appending comprehensive lists of required legal formalities and a draft SCAPIN.
subfiles.title: Staff Study: Direct Communication by Japanese Government with Persons Abroad in regard to Personal Status Matters
subfiles.to: Chief of Staff, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: This Japanese government memorandum proposes resolving 700,000 overseas personal status cases through direct correspondence, public information campaigns, and dispatching expert consular personnel.
subfiles.from: Eiji Wajima, Director of the Bureau of Control, Ministry of Foreign Affairs
subfiles.summary: Proposes direct correspondence, publication of regulations, and sending expert personnel abroad to resolve backlogged personal status notifications and protect overseas property interests.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Personal Status of Overseas Japanese
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: This monograph surveys the legal status, population statistics, repatriation problems, and treatment of Japanese settlers in detached territories and former colonial subjects residing in Japan.
subfiles.from: Foreign Office, Japanese Government
subfiles.summary: This monograph provides extensive demographic, historical, and occupational statistics on Japanese civilian settlers in former colonial territories including Korea, Formosa, Kwantung Leased Territory, Saghalien, and the Kurile Islands, as well as Korean and Formosan populations in Japan. It analyzes the severe property losses and humanitarian challenges attending civilian repatriation and the retention of technical specialists in North Korea. Furthermore, it discusses post-war problems concerning Korean residents in Japan, proposing that peace treaty arrangements follow European precedents by granting an option of nationality coupled with repatriation for those choosing foreign citizenship.
subfiles.title: Japanese Monograph: Japanese Nationals in Detached Territories and the Peoples of Those Territories Residing in Japan
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
